:::{#thm-cdf-derivative-is-density}
#### The derivative of the CDF is the density where the density is continuous

If $X$ is a continuous random variable with density $f$ and CDF $\cdf$,
then at every $t$ where $f$ is continuous:

$$f(t) = \deriv{t} \cdff{t}$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-density-vs-CDF, $\cdff{t} = \int_{-\infty}^{t} f(x)\,dx$.
The fundamental theorem of calculus then gives
$\deriv{t} \int_{-\infty}^{t} f(x)\,dx = f(t)$
at every $t$ where $f$ is continuous.

:::
